It was the [[List of FA Cup finals|145th final]] of English football's primary cup competition, the [[FA Cup|Football Association Challenge Cup]]. Chelsea played in their 17th FA Cup final and the first since [[2022 FA Cup final|2022]], when they lost for a record third consecutive time.{{Cite web |date=26 April 2026|title=Chelsea reach FA Cup final with 1-0 win over Leeds United |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/sport/football/chelsea-reach-fa-cup-final-with-1-0-win-over-leeds?ref=top-stories |agency=[[Reuters]] |access-date=26 April 2026|website=[[The Straits Times]] }} They were seeking a ninth Cup title. Manchester City played in their 15th FA Cup final overall and the fourth consecutively, the first ever team to do so.{{Cite web |date=25 April 2026|title=Man City fight back to beat Southampton and reach fourth straight FA Cup final |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/sport/football/man-city-fight-back-to-beat-southampton-and-reach-fourth-straight-fa-cup-final |agency=Reuters|access-date=25 April 2026|website=[[The Straits Times]] }} They were seeking an eighth Cup title. The clubs' most recent meeting in a title-deciding match was the [[2021 UEFA Champions League final]], which Chelsea won 1–0. The two sides have never before met in an FA Cup final, but have clashed in other domestic title-deciding matches, most recently in the [[2019 EFL Cup final]] and the [[2018 FA Community Shield]], both of which City won. They met twice in the [[2025–26 Premier League|season's Premier League]], a 1–1 draw in Manchester followed by City's 3–0 win in London. Manchester City won 1–0 in the match, through a goal from [[Antoine Semenyo]], achieving their 8th FA Cup title.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/48785885/chelsea-man-city-live-latest-updates-fa-cup-final-commentary-score-result |title=Chelsea vs Man City: Antoine Semenyo scores the winner as Man City lift FA Cup - as it happened |publisher=ESPN |date=16 May 2026 }} ==Route to the final== {{main|2025–26 FA Cup}} ===Chelsea===
{| class="wikitable plainrowheaders" style="text-align:center;margin:0" |- |+Chelsea's route to the final |- !scope="col" style="width:25px"|Round !scope="col" style="width:180px"|Opposition !scope="col" style="width:70px"|Score |- !scope=row style="text-align:center"|3rd |[[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] ([[The Valley (stadium)|A]]) |5–1 |- !scope=row style="text-align:center"|4th |[[Hull City F.C.|Hull City]] ([[MKM Stadium|A]]) |4–0 |- !scope=row style="text-align:center"|5th |[[Wrexham A.F.C.|Wrexham]] ([[Racecourse Ground|A]]) |4–2 {{aet}} |- !scope=row style="text-align:center"|QF |[[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]] ([[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|H]]) |7–0 |- !scope=row style="text-align:center"|SF |[[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] ([[Wembley Stadium|N]]) |1–0 |- |colspan="3"|'''Key:''' (H) = Home venue; (A) = Away venue; (N) = [[Neutral venue]] |}
As a Premier League team, [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] entered the tournament in the third round, beginning their FA Cup campaign with a dominant 5–1 away victory over Championship side [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]], in what was [[Liam Rosenior]]'s first match in charge of the club. Goals came from [[Tosin Adarabioyo]], [[Marc Guiu]], [[Pedro Neto]], [[Enzo Fernández]], and [[Jorrel Hato]], the latter scoring his first for Chelsea.{{cite web |title=Chelsea begin Rosenior era with FA Cup rout of Charlton |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/762514 |work=ESPN|date=10 January 2026 |access-date=26 April 2026}} Pedro Neto notched his first Chelsea hat-trick in the fourth round away to [[Hull City F.C.|Hull City]]. [[Estêvão Willian|Estêvão]] also contributed to the scoring, the match finishing 4–0 to the Blues.{{cite web |title=Pedro Neto hat trick sees Chelsea cruise to win at Hull in FA Cup |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/401850946 |work=ESPN|date=13 February 2026 |access-date=26 April 2026}} In the fifth round, Chelsea were drawn away yet again, this time against Championship club [[Wrexham A.F.C.|Wrexham]], who proved to be much tougher opposition than those in previous rounds. [[Sam Smith (footballer, born 1998)|Sam Smith]] and [[Callum Doyle]] got their names on the scoresheet for the Welsh club, with a late [[Josh Acheampong]] goal forcing extra time. [[Alejandro Garnacho]] and [[João Pedro (footballer, born 2001)|João Pedro]] both scored in extra time to secure a 4–2 win for Chelsea.{{cite web |title=Chelsea end Wrexham's FA Cup run in extra time |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/401861589 |work=ESPN|date=7 March 2026 |access-date=26 April 2026}} In the quarter-finals, Chelsea were drawn against tournament underdogs [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]]. Chelsea made light work of the League One side, defeating them 7–0 at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]], their largest FA Cup victory since [[2010–11 FA Cup|2011]], where Chelsea eased past [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] by the same scoreline.{{cite web |title=Chelsea 7-0 Ipswich (Jan 9, 2011) Final Score |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/310125/ipswich-town-chelsea |work=ESPN |date=9 January 2011 |access-date=26 April 2026}} Jorrel Hato, João Pedro, Tosin Adarabioyo, [[Andrey Santos]], Estêvão, and Alejandro Garnacho all found the net during the match, along with an own goal from Port Vale defender [[Jordan Lawrence-Gabriel]].{{cite web |title=Chelsea hammer Port Vale 7-0 in FA Cup quarterfinal |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/401864076 |work=ESPN |date=4 April 2026 |access-date=26 April 2026}} Chelsea faced Premier League rivals [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] in the semi-finals at Wembley, where a lone goal from Enzo Fernández was enough to secure a 1–0 victory and send the Blues to the FA Cup final. Chelsea is seeking their first FA Cup victory since beating [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] 1–0 in [[2018 FA Cup final|2018]].{{cite web |title=Chelsea v Leeds United: FA Cup semi-final – live |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/apr/26/chelsea-v-leeds-fa-cup-semi-final-live |work=The Guardian |date=26 April 2026 |access-date=26 April 2026}} ===Manchester City===
{| class="wikitable plainrowheaders" style="text-align:center;margin:0" |- |+Manchester City's route to the final |- !scope="col" style="width:25px"|Round !scope="col" style="width:180px"|Opposition !scope="col" style="width:70px"|Score |- !scope=row style="text-align:center"|3rd |[[Exeter City F.C.|Exeter City]] ([[City of Manchester Stadium|H]]) |10–1 |- !scope=row style="text-align:center"|4th |[[Salford City F.C.|Salford City]] ([[City of Manchester Stadium|H]]) |2–0 |- !scope=row style="text-align:center"|5th |[[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] ([[St James' Park|A]]) |3–1 |- !scope=row style="text-align:center"|QF |[[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] ([[City of Manchester Stadium|H]]) |4–0 |- !scope=row style="text-align:center"|SF |[[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] ([[Wembley Stadium|N]]) |2–1 |- |colspan="3"|'''Key:''' (H) = Home venue; (A) = Away venue; (N) = [[Neutral venue]] |}
As a Premier League team, [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] entered the tournament in the third round. City began their FA Cup campaign with a rampant 10–1 display at home against League One side [[Exeter City F.C.|Exeter City]]. Manchester City's ten goals came from seven different players and two own goals, with [[Rico Lewis]] scoring two goals, and [[Jake Doyle-Hayes]] and [[Jack Fitzwater]] each scoring an own goal. [[Max Alleyne]], [[Rodri (footballer, born 1996)|Rodri]], [[Antoine Semenyo]], [[Tijjani Reijnders]], [[Nico O'Reilly]], and [[Ryan McAidoo]] all scored for the home team, with [[George Birch (footballer)|George Birch]] scoring a consolation for Exeter.{{cite web |title=Antoine Semenyo scores as Man City thrash Exeter 10-1 |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/762497 |work=ESPN |date=10 January 2026 |access-date=26 April 2026}} This was their biggest win since defeating [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]] by the same score in 1987. City next faced [[Salford City F.C.|Salford City]] at home in the fourth round, and a goal from [[Marc Guéhi]] and an own goal from [[Alfie Dorrington]] helped overcome the League Two side to reach the fifth round, winning 2–0.{{cite web |title=City seal place in FA Cup fifth round with Salford victory |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/manchester-city-202526-salford-city-match-report-63906672 |publisher=Manchester City |date=14 February 2026 |access-date=26 April 2026}} In the fifth round, City defeated fellow Premier League side [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] 3–1 at [[St James' Park]]. Despite an opener from Newcastle's [[Harvey Barnes]], City came back due to two goals by [[Omar Marmoush]], and a goal from [[Savinho]].{{cite web |title=Omar Marmoush brace sees City ease past Newcastle into FA Cup quarterfinals |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/401861586 |work=ESPN |date=7 March 2026 |access-date=26 April 2026}} In the quarter-finals, Manchester City were drawn against eight-time cup winners [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], facing them at home. An [[Erling Haaland]] hat-trick and a goal from Antoine Semenyo helped City run out 4–0 victors, easing into their eighth FA Cup semi-final in a row.{{cite web |title=Haaland bags hat-trick as Man City hammer Liverpool 4-0 in FA Cup quarter-final |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/haaland-bags-hat-trick-man-city-hammer-liverpool-4-0-fa-cup-quarter-final-2026-04-04/ |agency=Reuters |date=4 April 2026 |access-date=26 April 2026}} Despite a 79th minute goal from [[Finn Azaz]], City defeated Championship side [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] 2–1 in the semi-finals at Wembley, as City mounted a late comeback through goals from [[Jérémy Doku]] and [[Nico González (footballer, born 2002)|Nico González]]. This marked the first time any team has reached four consecutive FA Cup finals, having previously played in the [[2023 FA Cup final|2023]], [[2024 FA Cup final|2024]] and [[2025 FA Cup final|2025]] finals respectively. ==Match== ===Summary=== In the 72nd minute, Manchester City scored the only goal of the match when [[Antoine Semenyo]] back flicked the ball with his right leg into the left corner of the net after a low cross from the right from [[Erling Haaland]].{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/16/manchester-city-win-fa-cup-final-as-semenyo-magic-sinks-chelsea|title= Manchester City win FA Cup final as Semenyo’s moment of magic floors Chelsea|date=16 May 2026|work=Guardian|accessdate=22 May 2026}} It was the only goal of the game as Manchester City won the game 1–0 and completed the domestic cup double after also winning the [[2026 EFL Cup final]] in March.{{cite web|url= https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-manchester-city/report/555725|title= Chelsea 0-1 Man City: Antoine Semenyo's brilliant flick seals FA Cup win and
